observation_summary: Several tests expecting double default values fail: either an assertion shows 0 (integer) instead of 0.0 (double) or a ClassCastException occurs (Integer cannot be cast to Double). The fix changes the literal used when inserting the double default into a map.
reasoning_summary: The fix replaces the integer literal 0 with the double literal 0D when populating primitive default values (primitiveValues.put(double.class, 0) -> primitiveValues.put(double.class, 0D)). This is a wrong value/initialization for the double entry causing wrong runtime type (Integer) and failed expectations. The change is a simple value/initialization correction, so Assignment/Initialization is the best ODC classification.
evidence_used: failing_tests: ClassCastException: java.lang.Integer cannot be cast to java.lang.Double
test snippets: assertions expecting 0.0D for double return values (HandyReturnValuesTest and ReturnsEmptyValuesTest)
evidence_gaps: No other modified files or wider context shown beyond the single-line change; however the diff is sufficient to identify the root cause.
No full production file content provided except the diff patch; line numbers/context are minimal but adequate for this classification.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The failure is not due to a missing or incorrect guard/condition; it is caused by inserting the wrong literal/type into the map, not by missing validation.
There is no procedural or algorithmic logic change—only a literal value changed. The algorithm remains the same.
This is not a boundary/contract mismatch between components; it's an internal initialization of a default value.
No concurrency, ordering, or synchronization change; the bug is a type/value error.
No broken association among structures or procedures is evident; the map entry had the wrong typed value.
The fix does not add or redesign a capability or class; it corrects a local initialization value.
